content.title: About
content.content: Soup, Hot and Sour (1909) is a classic Asian broth known for its bright tangy‑spicy flavor. Made from chicken or vegetable stock, it is seasoned with soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, garlic, chili peppers and often includes tofu, mushrooms, seaweed and scallions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish earned its name in the early 20th century when Beijing restaurants began experimenting with the balance of sour and hot.
It is traditionally served with rice noodles or plain rice, and sometimes topped with a poached egg.
Original recipes use rice vinegar, but many regions substitute lemon or lime juice.
Spiciness is adjusted with the amount of chili paste (e.g., Sichuan sauce) or fresh chilies.
The soup is considered a “warming” dish, often served in cold weather to boost body heat.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Ingredients such as tofu and mushrooms provide B1, B2 and B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Garlic and ginger have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Moderate amounts of soy sauce can help reduce LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Vinegar stimulates gastric juice production, while spices accelerate digestive processes.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The broth supplies fluids and electrolytes, especially beneficial in chilly climates.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant salt; low‑sodium versions are recommended for people with hypertension.

items.title: Spicy food sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of chili can irritate the stomach in individuals with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu and soy sauce may trigger allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Acid reflux
items.content: Vinegar and hot spices can exacerbate heartburn symptoms.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the hot soup in a deep bowl, garnish with fresh scallions, cilantro and lime wedges. Optional toppings include a boiled egg, fried tofu cubes, or seaweed for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water or broth to restore the desired consistency.
